title: SPA/183/2014 of Smt Manju Verma Vs Union Of India AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 183 of 2014
Smt. Manju Verma. ........... Appellant
Versus
Union of India & others. ............. Respondents
Mr. Siddhartha Sah, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Advocate for respondent Nos. 2 & 3.
JUDGMENT
Coram: Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.

BARIN GHOSH, C. J. (Oral)
 In 2010, appellant was transferred from Dehradun to Patna. She
accepted the transfer; joined at Patna; and, at the same time, retained the
quarter at Dehradun that was allotted to her. No sooner steps were taken
to recover penal rent in respect of the said quarter, appellant challenged
the order of transfer, which had been acted upon, or, in the alternative,
contended that a mandamus be issued directing her to be returned from
Patna principally on the ground that, at Patna, there is no post, where the
appellant can be suitably accommodated. A further contention was raised
in the writ petition pertaining to right of the appellant to obtain house rent
allowance at Patna. The writ petition has been disposed of by permitting
the appellant to make an appropriate representation pertaining to all her
grievances. Hence, this appeal.
2. The respondent / employer has various establishments throughout
India. Appellant was holding a transferable post. She, therefore, could be
transferred to any other establishment of the respondent / employer situate
in India. She was transferred and she accepted the transfer. She is, now,
seeking a re-transfer and, that too, at Dehradun. She has no right to get
what she was seeking and, accordingly, no mandamus to that effect can be
issued, unless it is established that, apart from Dehradun, the other
establishments of the respondent / employer do not have any
establishment, where the post, in which the appellant was appointed, is in

2
existence. The question is, whether the post, in which she had been
appointed, is available at Patna or not. This question can be fruitfully
gone-in by the court having jurisdiction over Patna.
3. We, accordingly, refuse to admit the appeal; but, ignoring the
observations as above, we request the respondent / employer to decide,
one way or the other, the representation to be made by the appellant
within a month from the date of receipt of the representation. The appeal
is, accordingly, disposed of.
